title: I'm So Constipado (False Cognate Disaster)
style: comedy bossa nova samba, 110 BPM, deadpan male lead vocal, theatrical narrator intro, brass band, nylon string guitar, awkward silence comedic timing, pharmacy bell SFX, EN/ES/PT codeswitch, language-learning anthem, hooky chorus, big band horn freakout
lyrics:
[Intro — pharmacy bell DING, awkward silence]
Pharmacist: ¿Cómo está usted?
Tourist: Estoy muy constipado…
Pharmacist: [long pause] …señor, eso es un problema diferente.

[Verse 1 — bossa nova guitar, deadpan male lead]
Walked into a Madrid pharmacy with a runny nose
Said "estoy constipado" — confident, head held high
Pharmacist looked concerned, reached for a different shelf
Came back with something I will NOT describe to myself

[Pre-Chorus — backup singers harmonize]
Constipado in Spanish means a COLD
Constipado in English means SOMETHING ELSE, I'm told
Constipado in Portuguese means BLOCKED UP TIGHT
Three languages, three meanings, one humiliating night

[Chorus — full samba band kicks in]
I'm so constipado, I sneezed all over the queue
I'm so constipado, the pharmacist said "ew"
I'm so constipado, in three different ways
False cognate funeral, somebody pra-ay!

[Verse 2 — escalation]
Then I tried to compliment the chef — "muy excited!"
Said "estoy excitado" — wait, that's NOT what I cited
Excitado means AROUSED in Spanish, that's the trick
The waiter dropped my paella, I felt physically sick

[Pre-Chorus]
Embarazada means PREGNANT, not embarrassed at all
Molestar means BOTHER, not what you call
Sopa is SOUP, not soap, do not eat the bar
Ropa is CLOTHES, not rope, don't tie up the car

[Chorus]
I'm so constipado, I sneezed all over the queue
I'm so constipado, the pharmacist said "ew"
I'm so constipado, in three different ways
False cognate funeral, somebody pra-ay!

[Bridge — slow, confessional]
I learned my languages from a textbook from nineteen ninety-two
The textbook lied, the textbook lied, the textbook lied to you
Real Spanish, real Portuguese, they'll humble you fast
The constipado moment — a memory built to last

[Final Chorus — louder, brass freakout]
I'm so constipado, I sneezed all over the queue
I'm so constipado, the pharmacist said "ew"
I'm so constipado, in three different ways
False cognate funeral, somebody pra-ay!

[Outro — whispered]
Tengo un resfriado. I have a cold. That's the phrase. Use that phrase.
